claims.exact_statement: For D=10^200 and the finite integer Z defined by Eq. (7.10) of the supplied paper, the spin-summed absolute-ground-state density of the three-electron Coulomb Hamiltonian with two nuclei of charge Z at (0,0,+/-D/Z) is not the density of any ground-state ensemble of H_s(v)=sum_i(-Delta_i/2+v(r_i)) for any real spin-independent multiplicative v in L^{3/2}(R^3)+L^infinity(R^3).
assumptions: All analytic and spectral hypotheses established in source §§2-4, including fixed-parameter density translation limits and planar lower tail.
Weighted spectral gap (4.23), established at selected t=1/Z through the all-minimizer tests in §§7.1-7.2.
Ground-state ensembles are positive trace-class operators supported on the N=3 ground eigenspace; arbitrary complex spinors and degeneracy are allowed.
Candidate potential is real, spin independent, local/multiplicative, and belongs to L^{3/2}+L^infinity.
claims.status: source-reported theorem; §§4-7 internally reconstructed with no concrete gap found in this audit; not externally validated, formalized, or priority-cleared
claims.novelty_boundary: Nodal-plane asymptotic mechanisms and ensemble KS are prior. The asserted new interface is a finite Coulomb ground-state density, all-ensemble kinetic certificate, and exclusion of the complete L^{3/2}+L^infinity scalar local potential class. The theorem does not cover distributional, spin-dependent, nonlocal, or finite-basis generalized-KS operators and does not imply practical KS failure.
claims.costs: Z is proved finite by a supremum over auxiliary couplings and predicates quantifying all folded minimizers, but is not evaluated and has no effective numerical upper bound; no executable numerical certificate or physical validation is supplied.
claims.falsifier: An admissible v and a ground-state ensemble with the stated spin-summed density would contradict the theorem. A proof audit must also find a failure in the source-dependent §§2-4 estimates, the §7 all-minimizers charge selector, or the §§5-6 transfer/Agmon chain.
claims.next_gate: Independent domain-expert audit of §§2-4 Coulomb channel/tail estimates and §§4/7 uniformity over every folded minimizer, followed by an independently replayable certificate for one fixed selected charge.
checked_interfaces: The natural-spin-orbital 1-RDM obeys 0<=gamma<=I, giving the rank-two occupied-spin-space Pauli bound for arbitrary ensembles.
Energy equality puts the determinant in the hypothetical many-body ground eigenspace; a one-orbital spin substitution identifies the scalar potential up to a constant.
All escaping bounded-potential limits equal d+k^2/2; the exterior form bound and Agmon estimate force a weighted H^1 trace incompatible with the planar tail.

claims.exact_statement: For m continuous scalar readouts restricted to a smooth-admissible (m+1)-dimensional sphere of Lamé coefficient perturbations, Borsuk-Ulam yields antipodal distinct coefficient fields with identical readouts.
assumptions: The admissible perturbation sphere remains inside the ellipticity/regularity class.
The readout map from that sphere to R^m is continuous and uses exactly m scalar outputs.
claims.status: conditional finite-data nonidentifiability gate retained from the prior branch; not a physical measurement theorem
claims.novelty_boundary: Borsuk-Ulam is standard; no new topology claim. The result does not cover vector-valued/complex measurements, noisy acquisition, or determine the admissible perturbation radius for a specimen.
claims.costs: m readout coordinates and an (m+1)-dimensional admissible sphere; no noise, conditioning, or experimental cost model is included.
claims.falsifier: A continuous injective map from the specified antipodal sphere into R^m, or failure of the constructed sphere to remain in the stated admissible class, defeats this exact gate.
claims.next_gate: Specify a physical acquisition map, its noise/conditioning, and a certified admissible sphere before claiming engineering consequences.
